_comment: Stotras appendix. loc: verse range per edition (vu Traditional, ce Critical; null if absent). opening: first words of the start verse (per edition if they differ). gita: the same range in the Gītā reader. Checked by: python etl/stotras.py check

opening.vu: raśmimantaṃ samudyantaṃ devāsuranamaskṛtam

stotras.fame: The best-known stotra inside the Rāmāyaṇa, recited daily for victory, health and removal of sorrow; kasarabada calls it 'the only Stotram in entire Ramayana'.
stotras.cited: Yuddha 107 (hindupedia, kasarabada, Gita Press numbering); verses 1-2 narrate, 3 'rāma rāma mahābāho', 4-5 phalaśruti, 6-24 hymn proper, 25-27 benefits, 28-30 Rāma's recitation. Absent from critical edition (not found in ce 6.105 or anywhere).

opening.vu: bhavān nārāyaṇo devaḥ śrīmāṃś cakrāyudho vibhuḥ

stotras.fame: The classic Rāmāyaṇa passage revealing Rāma's identity as Viṣṇu; listed in stotra collections as 'Brahma-kṛta Rāma-stuti', with its own phalaśruti ('those who recite it suffer no defeat').
stotras.cited: Yuddha 117.13-33 on valmikiramayan.net / sanskritdocuments (Kumbhakonam-style numbering); Yuddha 120 in our vu. Verse 33/34 closing calls it 'imam ārṣaṃ stavam' (ce ends 29 with 'ye narāḥ kīrtayiṣyanti nāsti teṣāṃ parābhavaḥ').

opening.vu: tvāṃ niyokṣyāmahe viṣṇo lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā

stotras.fame: The petition that sets the Rāma avatāra in motion; treated as the gods' stuti of Viṣṇu in Bāla Kāṇḍa summaries.
stotras.cited: Bāla 15.18-26 (valmikiramayan.net: 'devas bowed and offered prayers'; 15.26 'evaṃ stutaḥ'). ce end estimated (verse 21 is the last of the gods' speech heard in heads).

opening.vu: putro daśarathasyāyaṃ mahārājasya dhīmataḥ

stotras.fame: Sītā's well-known invocation of Gaṅgā for Rāma's safe return after fourteen years, with praise of Gaṅgā as 'tripathagā' and consort of the ocean.
stotras.cited: Ayodhyā 52.83-91 (valmikiramayan.net); vu verse 82 narrates, ce 2.46.67 narrates; ce lacks the vu's extra vow verses 89-90.

opening.vu: namo 'stu rāmāya salakṣmaṇāya

stotras.fame: Frequently chanted single-verse salutation of Hanumān, recited in Sundara Kāṇḍa pārāyaṇa as a prayer for success; the page itself does not label it a stotra.
stotras.cited: Sundara 13.59 (sanskritdocuments/valmikiramayan.net, shlokam.org 'Namostu Ramaya Sa'); a single verse, popularly chanted on its own.

stotras.name_en: Sītā's prayer to Agni for Hanumān

opening.vu: yadyasti patiśuśrūṣā yadyasti caritaṃ tapaḥ

stotras.fame: Well-known satya-based invocation, quoted as an example of the power of Sītā's pativratā truth; chanted for protection from fire.
stotras.cited: Sundara 53.27-31 (vedapath.app 5.53.28 shows 'yady asti patiśuśrūṣā... śīto bhava hanūmataḥ'); vu verse 27 narrates the invocation.

opening.vu: yaṃ pālayasi dharmaṃ tvaṃ dhṛtyā ca niyamena ca

stotras.fame: The classic mother's maṅgalāśīr/svastyayana; recited as a protective blessing for travellers, resembling a stotra of the Maṅgalāśāsana type.
stotras.cited: Ayodhyā 25.2-26 (valmikiramayan.net: 'blessings and svastivācana'; 26 'stutibhiḥ anurūpābhiḥ'); ce lacks vu verse 3 'dharmastvām abhirakṣatu' and begins at 'svasti sādhyāś ca viśve ca'.

opening.vu: viśvaṃ viṣṇur vaṣaṭkāro bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ

stotras.fame: The most recited stotra of the epic, taught by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira; core text of daily Vaiṣṇava recitation with Śaṅkara's commentary.
stotras.cited: Anuśāsana 149 (Gita Press, Kumbhakonam-type counts differ), 13.135 (BORI); in our vu 13.254

opening.vu: ārirādhayiṣuḥ kṛṣṇaṃ vācaṃ jigadiṣāmi yām

stotras.fame: Bhīṣma's dying-on-the-bed-of-arrows hymn to Kṛṣṇa, traditionally called Stavarāja, recited as an independent Vaiṣṇava stotra with its own commentaries and manuscripts.
stotras.cited: Śānti 47 (Gita Press; Leipzig MyMss record Śāntiparvan ch. 47), 12.47 (BORI); in our vu 12.46 [opening note: preceded by śuciṃ śucipadaṃ haṃsaṃ at 12.46.18 vu / 12.47.11 ce]

opening.vu: tvāmekamāhuḥ puruṣaṃ tvāmāhuḥ sātvatāṃ patim

stotras.fame: Yudhiṣṭhira's thanksgiving litany of Kṛṣṇa's names and forms after his abhiṣeka; circulated as a separate Kṛṣṇa stotra. DOUBTFUL as 'well known': end verse not fixed, page not read.
stotras.cited: Śānti 42 (vu) / 12.43 (BORI); sanskritdocuments has it as 'yudhiṣṭhirakṛtaṃ 1 śrīkṛṣṇastotram' (title seen in search results only; page not retrievable) [opening note: namaste... at 12.42.3]

stotras.name_en: Thousand names of Śiva, taught by Taṇḍi

opening.vu: sthiraḥ sthāṇuḥ prabhur bhānuḥ pravaro varado varaḥ

stotras.fame: The standard Śivasahasranāma (also in Śivapurāṇa/Liṅgapurāṇa variants), taught by Kṛṣṇa after Upamanyu; widely printed in Śaiva stotra collections.
stotras.cited: Anuśāsana 17 (Gita Press; Leipzig record 'Śivasahasranāma, Anuśāsanaparvan 17'), 13.17 (BORI); in our vu 13.48

opening.vu: namaste devadeveśa devāribalasūdana

stotras.fame: Second Mahābhārata Śivasahasranāma, sung by Dakṣa after Śiva's grace in the Dakṣa-yajña episode; printed as 'Dakṣaproktaṃ śivasahasranāmastotram'.
stotras.cited: Śānti 284 (Gita Press, Dakṣa-yajña/Jvarotpatti section; chapter number from memory, not confirmed by a fetched source); our vu 12.290; BORI places it in an appendix to 12.274 [ce: appendix insertion, whole text lumped in one verse]

opening.vu: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitras tvaṃ gatir gatimatāṃ vara

stotras.fame: Short stava with which Taṇḍi pleased Śiva, the narrative prelude to the sahasranāma; printed as 'Taṇḍikṛtaṃ Śivastotram'. Less famous than the sahasranāma (marked doubtful).
stotras.cited: Anuśāsana 16 (BORI), vu 13.47; sanskritdocuments title 'taṇḍirṣikṛtaṃ śivastotram' seen in search results

opening.vu: namo devādhidevāya mahādevāya vai namaḥ

stotras.fame: Kṛṣṇa's account to Yudhiṣṭhira of how he worshipped Śiva at Upamanyu's āśrama; end verse a rough estimate. Doubtful as separate known stotra.
stotras.cited: Anuśāsana 14 (BORI), vu 13.45; sanskritdocuments 'kṛṣṇakṛtaṃ 4 śivastotram' (title seen only in search results, not read)

opening.vu: namo 'stu te śāśvata sarvayone brahmādhipaṃ tvām ṛṣayo vadanti

stotras.fame: Kṛṣṇa's 'tvaṃ vai brahmā ca rudraś ca' praise of Sthāṇu after the vision; end verse estimated. Doubtful as separate known stotra.
stotras.cited: Anuśāsana 15 (BORI), vu 13.45; sanskritdocuments Kṛṣṇakṛta Śivastotra series (title only)

opening.vu: namostu varade kṛṣṇe kumāri brahmacāriṇi

stotras.fame: Yudhiṣṭhira's hymn to Durgā on entering Virāṭa's city, who grants victory; one of the best known Durgā stotras, frequently printed as 'Yudhiṣṭhirakṛtaṃ Durgāstavam'.
stotras.cited: Virāṭa 6 (Gita Press, Ganguly/Krishnakosh Virāṭa 6); sanskritdocuments 'Durgā-stava mahābhārāntargata', Virāṭaparva ch. 8 (southern recension), 'Durgā nakṣatramālikā stuti' with 27 or 36 verses [CE: absent from main text; hymn in appendix/not found] [opening note: intro yaśodāgarbhasaṃbhūtāṃ nārāyaṇavarapriyām]

opening.vu: namas te siddhasenāni ārye mandaravāsini

stotras.fame: Kṛṣṇa tells Arjuna to pray to Durgā for victory just before the Gītā; extremely popular 'Durgā Stuti' in Devī collections.
stotras.cited: Bhīṣma Parva 23 (Gita Press, ramanuja.org, shastras.com, mahabharataonline); our vu 6.23; BORI relegates to appendix inside 6.22 [ce: lumped appendix text]

opening.vu: tvaṃ bhāno jagataś cakṣus tvam ātmā sarvadehinām

stotras.fame: Dhaumya's 108 names of the Sun with which Yudhiṣṭhira gained the inexhaustible Akṣayapātra; recited as Sūryāṣṭottaraśata.
stotras.cited: Āraṇyaka/Vana Parva 3 (Ganguly/Krishnakosh Vana 3); sanskritdocuments 'sūryāṣṭottaraśatanāmāvaliḥ' [vu: hymn 17-67, names ~68-81] [ce: names; the preceding praise is lumped at 3.3.14] [vu hymn 3.3.17-67, names 68-81; ce names 18-29, praise lumped at 3.3.14] [opening note: names from sūryo 'ryamā bhagas tvaṣṭā pūṣārkaḥ savitā raviḥ]

opening.vu: prapūrvagau pūrvajau citrabhānū girā vāṃ śaṃsāmi tapasā hyanantau

stotras.fame: Upamanyu's Ṛgvedic-style verses to the Aśvins that restore his sight; classic Vedic-flavoured hymn inside the epic.
stotras.cited: Ādi 3 (Paushya/Utathya story; Gita Press 1.3, BORI 1.3)

opening.vu: tvam ṛṣis tvaṃ mahābhāgas tvaṃ devaḥ patageśvaraḥ

stotras.fame: Gods praise Garuḍa when he blazes like fire while carrying off the amṛta; the nucleus of later Garuḍa stotras.
stotras.cited: Ādi 20 (BORI/Pune) = 1.23 in our vu (Āstīka/Garuḍa story)

opening.vu: namas te sarvadeveśa namas te balasūdana

stotras.fame: Kadrū praises Indra so that rain will relieve her sun-scorched snake sons; short eulogy that is nature-hymn in form.
stotras.cited: Ādi 21 (BORI), 1.25 in our vu [opening note: ce: namas te devadeveśa...]

opening.vu: kapardin sarvabhūteśa bhaganetranipātana

stotras.fame: Arjuna recognises Śiva as the hunter and prays; the episode that wins him the Pāśupata.
stotras.cited: Vana 39 (Gita Press; Kirātārjunīya part), BORI 3.40

stotras.name_en: Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna's hymn to Rudra

opening.vu: namo bhavāya śarvāya rudrāya varadāya ca paśūnāṃ pataye nityam ugrāya ca kapardine

stotras.fame: Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna praise Śiva in the lake visit that wins the Pāśupatāstra before Jayadratha's death; a popular Rudra stotra.
stotras.cited: Droṇa 80 (vu) / 7.57 (BORI), 'Śiva-sahasranāma/Śivastuti within the Pāśupata journey; sanskritdocuments 'kṛṣṇārjunābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ rudrastotram' (title seen in search results only)

opening.vu: ugraṃ sthāṇuṃ śivaṃ rudraṃ śarvam īśānam īśvaram

stotras.fame: Aśvatthāman offers himself as oblation to Śiva before the night massacre; short, powerful, and often cited in Advaita-l/Śaiva discussion.
stotras.cited: Sauptika Parva 7.2-11 (sanskritdocuments transcription 'drauṇikṛtaṃ rudrastotram'); BORI 10.7

opening.vu: namaste devadeveśa niṣkriya nirguṇa lokasākṣin kṣetrajña puruṣottama

stotras.fame: The long litany of about 170 epithets in the Nārāyaṇīya, sung before Nārada's vision of the universal form; included in Pāñcarātra/Vaiṣṇava stotra collections.
stotras.cited: Śānti 339 (Ganguly/KMG Nārāyaṇīya), 12.325 (BORI, verse 4 numbered 12325004A-Q), our vu 12.346

opening.vu: āgneyaś ca skandaś ca dīptakīrtir anāmayaḥ

stotras.fame: Mārkaṇḍeya's list of Skanda's names with phalaśruti, source of the popular Skanda nāmāvali.
stotras.cited: Vana 3.233 (Kumbhakonam edition per studylearningcircle); Vana 232 in other numberings (Ganguly) — not resolved [CE: absent from main text; hymn in appendix/not found] [opening note: intro bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi nāmāni ca mahātmanaḥ]

stotras.name_en: Arjuna's hymn to the Universal Form

opening.vu: sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā jagat prahṛṣyaty anurajyate ca

stotras.fame: Arjuna's awed hymn (11.36 sthāne, 11.40 namaḥ purastāt) is recited separately and in Viśvarūpa stotra collections.
stotras.cited: Bhagavadgītā 11.15-46 (inside Bhīṣma Parva 6.35 vu / 6.33 BORI) – in the Gītā, not a stand-alone epic episode [opening note: vision begins paśyāmi devāṃs tava deva dehe, 11.15]
